validation_note: All 526 districting and script regression tests passed in 11.13 seconds. Browser checks passed for the comparison, harbor and island views, Ellis land crossing, and link/context toggles, with no captured browser errors or warnings. Source-map screenshots are saved beside the comparison. Both orchestrators and all four benchmark children have exited; the state36 execution lock was independently verified free.

strict_baseline.note: K35/K42/K61 reused the K26 source-topology rejection. No prior strict solver runtimes or population results exist.

isolated_island_water_access.interpretation: Positive separation means any connection from this source block to mapped harbor water must first cross a nonwater gap.
The source block boundary reaches mapped harbor water.

geographic_explanation.liberty_island: Liberty Island belongs to New York, while surrounding water belongs to New Jersey under the 1834 compact. Its nearest selected boundary connection is mapped water-only.
geographic_explanation.ellis_island: The original Ellis Island and main building belong to New York; most expanded island area belongs to New Jersey. The Census New York source block is enclosed by mapped New Jersey land, so the proposed connection includes a short land crossing.

conditional_partition_extension.statement: Any valid part-connected partition of the main source component extends to these islands by assigning both zero-population island blocks to the district containing the common anchor block. Every district population stays unchanged, and the two recorded links connect that district under the augmented policy.
conditional_partition_extension.prerequisite: Explicit permission for the Ellis cross-New-Jersey-land exclave link, as well as the Liberty water link.
conditional_partition_extension.limits: This conditional construction does not produce or prove the quality/existence of a balanced main-component district plan. Physical polygon connectivity remains separate, and full graph/polygon-plus-link validation remains necessary.

record.measurement: Local equirectangular lengths of exact source-polygon intersections. Overlapping intersections are merged as normalized intervals; no geometry is buffered or repaired.
limits: Area-water is mapped 2020 geography, not present water levels or navigability.
Connection lines are graph-policy proposals, not existing roads, bridges, ferries, or changes to state boundaries.
Water/land classification is independent of population-aware graph selection and final district validation.
Context display polygons are clipped and simplified; calculations use full unsimplified source geometry.

measurement_notes: New plans run serially in fresh processes with cached source and part graphs; shared-desktop timings are observations, not isolated hardware comparisons.

For accepted plans, pipeline time includes source and link preparation, solving, repair/rebalance, independent polygon validation, map export, viewer generation and preservation checks. For failed attempts it measures only work through the failed phase plus failure cleanup/preservation; unexecuted repair or export phases are not included.
Process imports, initial preservation inventory and final report flush are outside the pipeline timer.
Strict topology rejection happened before solving; it is not a before/after solver-performance baseline.

Physical shared-edge connectivity and policy connectivity are separate. Liberty uses a water link; Ellis uses an explicit exclave link over New Jersey land and water. No New Jersey area or population is assigned.

Only accepted-plan population deviations are independently recomputed from source DBF and final assignments. Failed attempts have no accepted final balance or district-connectivity measurement. Local whole-block balancing does not establish global optimality.

Successful inner optimizer passes, outer center convergence, final postprocessed population balance and policy connectivity are independent outcomes. Outer iteration-limit cases are disclosed explicitly.
Compressed payloads measure saved map bytes, not browser memory or latency. New Jersey diagnostic context loads only on connection/harbor inspection and is separate from the map export sizes.
